scope: Read-only existing WSL CPU/sysfs/dmesg/config and WSA kernel embedded config; no AArch32 code executed
conclusion: N1X uses Cortex-X925 and Cortex-A725 cores; Arm primary sources describe both as AArch64-only. Native AArch32 execution cannot be enabled by merely changing the WSA kernel or Android ABI properties.

limitations: WSL reports a virtual CPU view: all 20 vCPUs report 0xd85, so this is not a physical core topology measurement.
Neither /proc/cpuinfo Features nor MIDR directly encodes the AArch32 EL0 capability. MIDR identifies a CPU model; source documentation supplies its capability.

ID_AA64PFR0_EL1 was not measured; the standard sysfs identification directory exposes MIDR/AIDR/REVIDR only. Linux userspace MRS feature exposure masks fields, and a hypervisor may constrain the guest view.
No 32-bit EL0 line was found in captured WSL dmesg; absence alone is not used to establish physical hardware capability.
The old WSA kernel and current WSL kernel both have CONFIG_COMPAT=y; this is compatibility code, not CPU instruction-set emulation.
WSA ENOEXEC alone cannot distinguish missing CPU/virtualization/kernel support. Hardware conclusion comes from NVIDIA topology and Arm core documentation.

sources.fact: N1X 20-core model has 10 Cortex-X925 performance and 10 Cortex-A725 efficiency cores.
Arm source marks Cortex-X925 a 64-bit-only core and rejects AArch32 register context.
Userspace ID register values are system-safe, filtered, and may reflect kernel support rather than complete physical capabilities.
Linux may reject AArch32 ELF with ENOEXEC where no usable compatible CPU exists; software emulation/recompilation are separate alternatives.
